chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Bukayr, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The garment does not render the man junub, and the man does not render the garment junub.

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment as the object of the ruling
key_terms.الرَّجُلَ: the man, meaning the person in this ruling
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man, as the one in the state being discussed
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: causes to be in a state of janabah or renders ritually impure in that sense

ai.seo_question: Does a garment become junub when touched by a person in janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning ritual purity: the state of janabah does not transfer between a person and a garment merely through contact. It indicates that a garment itself does not become described as junub, nor does touching such a garment place a person in janabah.
